scoringCalibration: The undercut density layer earns one visual point because it removes exposed scalp bands without changing the weak primary groom silhouette.
visualFindings: The side and rear scalp now read as a deliberately faded short undercut instead of exposed skin beneath a disconnected cap.
Vertex-authored density reaches zero at the side and lower boundaries, removing the rectangular and jagged silhouettes seen in v31 and v32.
The new layer remains underneath the existing large hair mass and boundary fibers, so the front silhouette and v30 facial work are unchanged.
The crown still reads as uniformly combed strands over a smooth cap and the haircut still lacks convincing large and medium clump design.
rejectedExperiments: v31 was rejected because copied body-face selection produced jagged dark patches around the ears and rear scalp.
v32 was rejected because the continuous projected shell still rendered as an opaque hard-edged block.
blockingFailures: The primary groom still needs hand-shaped large and medium clumps, a readable part, crown breakup and denser side volume.
A true mouth slit, oral cavity, teeth, tongue and expression-compatible lip topology are still missing.
Integrated eyelid thickness and high-resolution canthus anatomy remain below review quality.
Clothing edge flow, seams, folds, materials and outer layers remain below review quality.
Raised-arm shoulders still require corrective deformation and the standard pose suite remains incomplete.
Signed clothing-distance samples remain negative despite zero exact triangle overlaps in the two audited frames.
LOD transition popping and frame-time impact remain untested in the website renderer.
